rules: Clear a small, dry floor area. Keep paths away from stairs, doors, glass and furniture corners.
Walk indoors. Do not climb or jump on furniture.
Paper marks a station: stand beside it, not on it.
Use loose, soft rolled socks with nothing inside. Throw only at containers or cup targets, never at faces or bodies.
Stop throwing before anybody picks up socks.
Keep real doors unlocked. Pause for rest or water whenever needed. An adult stays involved throughout.
Do not search drawers, cupboards, electrical areas or anyone else’s belongings.

setup: Draw circle, star, triangle and square station cards, plus a ship/base. Put them beside clear walking routes.
Draw a visible map: circle → star → triangle (add square for ages 11–12).
Keep crystal one with you and crystal two at the final map station. Keep the toy and crystal three aside until stage 2B.
Make two paper loading-stop labels near the ship.
activity_home_missing_power_crystals.opening: Captain, our ship has landed on a strange planet. Three power crystals are missing. We must find all three and rescue our astronaut before we can fly home. Name our ship, then follow the first signal!

parts.read: Visit the planets in our map’s order and report back to mission control.
do: Walk beside the marks, return and check the route together.
Award crystal one after exploring. No speed or perfect memory needed.

bands.5-7: Two or three visible stations. Walk together first.
bands.8-10: Three stations. Look, cover the map, walk and check.
bands.11-12: Four stations. Plan the route and explain one choice.

parts.hint: Point to the next shape or walk together.

stages.title: Transport the second crystal and rescue

parts.label: A. Towel transport
parts.read: The second crystal is fragile. Our towel sling can carry it if we coordinate our movements. Which clear route should we take?
do: Hold opposite towel ends, carry crystal two together and park it at the ship.
If it falls, stop, replace it and carry on. Walk, without pulling against each other.

bands.5-7: Short straight route. The child calls go and stop.
bands.8-10: Choose a two-stop route and agree turning signals.
bands.11-12: Compare route options and explain which protects the load better.

parts.label: B. Rescue the astronaut and third crystal
parts.read: A signal from our astronaut! They have found the last crystal, but need our help. How will we bring both back?
do: Place the toy and crystal three at different stations.
Make separate trips for the toy and the crystal, returning each to the ship.

bands.5-7: You point to the two stations. The child chooses which to visit first.
bands.8-10: The child plans the two trips and tells mission control the order.
bands.11-12: The child revises the plan if one imaginary route closes. Another clear floor route must remain, with no furniture crossing.

stages.title: Load the ship, decode the launch and fly home

parts.label: A. Load the ship
parts.read: Everyone is safe and all three crystals are here. We need to move them through the loading stations and into the engine bay. You are in charge!
do: Place the crystals at a nearby collection point. The child chooses the clear route past the two loading-stop labels to the ship.
Move one crystal per trip and check all three arrive. Follow the child’s directions on at least one delivery, then swap roles.

bands.5-7: Choose between two routes you propose. You help count arrivals.
bands.8-10: Choose the loading-stop order and guide alternate deliveries.
bands.11-12: Decide an efficient route, explain it and adjust unclear directions.

parts.label: B. Decode the launch and fly home
parts.read: Our ship needs an action password. Teach mission control your code, check the crystals and lead the launch!
do: Choose comfortable actions such as marching on the spot, reaching or side-steps.
The child teaches a sequence. Rehearse, then perform it together after counting all three crystals.
Younger children: teach one action at a time, then join them.

bands.5-7: Choose two actions from your examples, then copy each other.
bands.8-10: Make three actions and teach you their order.
bands.11-12: Make four actions. Spot and correct your sequencing mistake.

stages.closing: All three crystals are loaded and our astronaut is safe. Engines on, we’re home! Tell me what we see through the window as we land. (The 20-minute story ends here.)

parts.read: We are home, but a new rescue signal has arrived! Our astronaut needs help on another planet. This time, you can change the map.
do: Reuse the toy and crystals. Move two station labels and plan a new clear route.
Alternate navigator and carrier. Try two rescue rounds and compare the routes.

bands.11-12: Declare one imaginary route closed and revise the plan.

do: The child designs a loading route and a new launch code with the same materials.
Test it with you following directions. Swap roles, change one unclear instruction and play again.
Close with another successful landing and tidy up together.

bands.5-7: Dictate a picture route and two actions.
bands.8-10: Use two loading stops and three actions.
bands.11-12: Add a delivery problem and four actions.

setup: Choose a short clear rolling lane and a gentle throwing direction away from breakable objects.
Use paper marks beside the feet for where to stand.
For 40 minutes, reuse the same six cups for the two snow forts.
activity_home_sock_ball_carnival.opening: Welcome to our home carnival! We have bowling and basketball today. (For 40 minutes add: Then we’ll open the snow forts and curling rink.)

do: Agree where to stand, where socks may travel and a shared retrieval signal.
Try gentle rolls and basket throws, adjusting the distance so success is possible. Demonstrate first, then let the child help set up the play area.
Choose cooperative scoring or friendly personal scores. Nobody is eliminated.
Arrange six cups. Each player rolls two socks, notes the cups knocked down, then retrieves and resets.
Play three rounds before changing the arrangement. Try a triangle and a line. Swap who arranges and who bowls.
Make the final round a shared goal, such as clearing all the pins using both players’ turns.
Too hard: shorten the distance or separate the pins. Too easy: change the layout before increasing distance. Retrieve only after rolling stops.

bands.5-7: Offer two nearby rolling spots. Count knocked cups together.
bands.8-10: The child arranges the pins and compares results across layouts.
bands.11-12: Test two layouts over three rounds each and explain which needs more control. Adjust each player’s distance to keep it fair.

stages.title: Sock basketball

do: Take turns with three gentle tosses each, then collect together. Start close, then try a second spot.
Change one thing per round: position, throwing hand if comfortable, or the scoring rule.
Finish with a shared goal chosen after the practice round, such as three baskets together with as many turns as needed.

bands.5-7: Basket nearby. You count shared successes, the child chooses the last spot.
bands.8-10: Two spots and alternating rounds. Choose an achievable team target.
bands.11-12: Design a scoring rule and fair distances, then revise after testing.

stages.closing: Our carnival is complete! Which game shall we bring back another day? Let’s collect our equipment together. (The 20-minute version ends here.)

do: Each player arranges three cups as a ground-level fort. Alternate one gentle throw at the other fort from agreed spots. The non-thrower waits outside the throwing lane.
After each has thrown three times, stop, collect and rebuild. Try a line, triangle or spaced pattern.
End by combining the cups into one fort and knocking it down together.
The cups are the only targets: no throwing at people, chasing or dodging.

bands.5-7: You help build. Use a close position and focus on aiming.
bands.8-10: The child chooses a new arrangement each round and compares outcomes.
bands.11-12: Predict which layout is harder to hit, test it, then redesign.

do: Lay a paper target at the end of the clear lane. Each player rolls three socks to stop near it.
Leave them in place until the round ends, compare distances by eye, then retrieve together. Try a new target position and swap who coaches.
If socks do not roll well, reshape them loosely or use a gentle underarm slide. No hard objects inside the socks.
Finish with a shared last round and choose a favourite carnival event while tidying up. No overall winner is needed.

bands.5-7: Aim to finish near the paper. Choose which sock landed closest.
bands.8-10: Adjust force after comparing three attempts. Try a joint target.
bands.11-12: Predict stopping points, test and coach you using observations.

setup: You are mission control, not an opponent. Play in a small designated area, never behind a locked door.
Make a base/control panel and three visible stations labelled STAR, CIRCLE and TRIANGLE with matching drawings.

Badge pieces: A “1: STAR” (start at CIRCLE), B “2: CIRCLE” (start at TRIANGLE), C “3: TRIANGLE” (start at STAR). Draw TRIANGLE on the back of A, STAR on the back of B, and “Return to base” on the back of C. Draw CIRCLE on a separate starting clue.
Code cards, held by you until stage 1B: STAR = 2, CIRCLE = 4, TRIANGLE = 1.
Final clue, handed over at CIRCLE after stage 2A: “Read the numbers in your badge route order.”
Action key, kept until stage 2B: 2 = two side-steps; 4 = four marching steps on the spot; 1 = one reach.
Write a delivery message: “Request the final access clue.”

Ages 11–12: replace the badge fronts with ordering clues: A = “CIRCLE comes immediately after STAR”; B = “TRIANGLE is last”; C = “Visit each symbol once”. Ages 5–7: lean on the drawings and read and count with the child.
activity_home_secret_agent_escape.opening: Agent, our pretend training base is in protection mode. We need your badge, an access code and an action password to reopen headquarters. You can ask mission control for a hint at any time. First, follow this circle clue.

stages.title: Recover the badge and collect the access code

parts.label: A. Recover the badge
do: The child walks to CIRCLE, finds A and brings it back. Its back sends them to TRIANGLE for B, then STAR for C. One piece per trip.
Put the pieces face up and work out the route for part B. Then explain that the fronts reveal a different route for the code cards.

bands.5-7: Go with the child on the first trip, point to pictures and help order the numbered fronts. Walk the assembled route together.
bands.8-10: The child follows the trail alone within the area, orders the fronts and rehearses before turning the cards over.
bands.11-12: The child solves the three ordering statements and explains the route.

parts.label: B. Collect the access code
parts.read: Your badge has revealed the patrol route. Visit those stations in order and bring their code cards to the control panel.
do: Correct route: STAR → CIRCLE → TRIANGLE.
Hand over the matching code card at each station. The child returns it to base before visiting the next. A wrong visit earns a hint and a retry, not a penalty.

bands.5-7: Route stays visible. You help match shapes and numbers.
bands.8-10: Look, remember the next station, walk there and return to check.
bands.11-12: Justify each station using the ordering clues. Audit your patrol and explain any correction.

stages.title: Deliver the request and learn the action key

parts.label: A. Deliver the request
parts.read: We have the numbers, but need the final instruction. Send this request to the correct station and bring back its reply.
do: Give the message and a destination clue. The answer is CIRCLE.
When the child delivers it there, hand over the final clue and have them return it to base. If stuck, point to the badge’s second symbol, then go with them.

bands.8-10: Say “Deliver to the second station in your badge route”.
bands.11-12: Show “Deliver to the second badge station” and the decoy “Deliver to TRIANGLE; it is the second badge station”. The child checks against the route and rejects the false claim.

parts.label: B. Learn the action key
parts.read: Our lock uses both numbers and movements. Let’s learn what each number means before trying the complete password.
do: Show the action key (2 = two side-steps; 4 = four marching steps; 1 = one reach). Match code cards to actions and practise each group in different orders.
Do not open headquarters yet. Teach one group at a time.

bands.5-7: You point and count aloud. The child copies each action group.
bands.8-10: The child matches numbers to movements and teaches each group.
bands.11-12: The child explains the mapping and corrects your rehearsal mistake.

stages.title: Solve the final code and escape

parts.read: Now use the final clue to put our cards in order. Say the number code, then lead us through its movements to open headquarters.
do: Route: STAR → CIRCLE → TRIANGLE. Code: 2–4–1.
Perform two side-steps, four marching steps on the spot and one reach together.

bands.5-7: You help arrange the symbols and count the actions with the child.
bands.8-10: The child orders the cards and leads the whole action password.
bands.11-12: The child explains the ordering evidence, then leads the password.

parts.hint: Offer hints freely, with no timer or penalty: (1) “Which symbol comes first on your badge?” (2) Point to STAR and its number. (3) Arrange STAR–CIRCLE–TRIANGLE and 2–4–1 together.

stages.closing: Access restored! Headquarters is open. Your team followed the clues and completed the password. Mission accomplished! The real door has stayed open. Tidy the props together. (The 20-minute version ends here.)

parts.read: Headquarters is open! Another team needs supplies. Can you plan a delivery and send a reply?
do: Reuse the route STAR → CIRCLE → TRIANGLE. First send supplies to CIRCLE, then to STAR.
Carry each of the two sock supplies there on a towel together, return to base, then swap dispatcher and carrier.
Let the child explain or point out the right destination before moving.

bands.5-7: Use the drawing of CIRCLE, then of STAR.
bands.8-10: Say “second route station” for CIRCLE, “first route station” for STAR.
bands.11-12: Use a verified instruction plus a false claim each time (for STAR: “TRIANGLE is the first route station”).

do: The child reorders the three stations into a new practice route. Write the answer first: for example CIRCLE → TRIANGLE → STAR means 4–1–2.
Write or draw clues, walk the trail to check it, then collect the code cards and try the new password. Repair unclear clues and replay that section.
Close with the action password and tidy up. No extra props or hidden locations needed.
